papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that defines benchmark dependence, a task-level generalization of Bell measurement dependence, proves a tight additive bound on how much benchmark-correlated side information can raise a classical score, and applies it to IBM hardware Bell-game data and to a Havlicek-style quantum-kernel benchmark.

existing.note: The stored quotes cut off the inequality. The body states it in full, with its conditions (reward in [0, 1]), shows it is independent of the number of parties and of the sizes of the input, output and hidden-variable spaces, and proves no universal bound with a sublinear penalty exists.
existing.value: The paper proves that for any distributed task with reward in [0, 1], the optimal classical score under benchmark dependence of strength at most η satisfies Sη ≤ min{1, Scl + η}, where Scl is the optimal benchmark-independent classical value; the bound is independent of the number of parties and of the sizes of the input, output and hidden-variable spaces. It constructs a family of tasks that saturates the bound and proves that no universal bound Sη ≤ Scl + g(η) with g(η) = o(η) as η → 0 holds for all bounded-reward tasks.
